posts.text: I'm excited to join Beacon Health (YC W26) as a Product Engineering Intern in New York City!🗽 Really grateful to all my family, friends, and mentors who have supported me, and thank you to Obinna and Mark for making this happen! Super stoked to be a part of this amazing team this winter!

We won LA Hacks. Our team built Edith, a real-time AI assistant that runs on Meta Ray-Ban glasses. You speak naturally, the glasses see what you see, and Edith handles the rest, looking up who you just met, sending follow-up emails, booking reservations, all without touching your phone. Built on Fetch.ai's OmegaClaw reasoning system and ASI Agentverse, Edith is not a voice interface. It is a fully agentic pipeline that interprets intent, delegates to specialized agents, and executes actions end

I'm excited to share that I’ll be joining Thales as a Data Science Intern in Ottawa this summer! Incredibly grateful to everyone who supported me along the way and helped make this possible. Excited for what’s ahead!

We built Vit. Version control for DaVinci Resolve. Git, but for video editors. Professional video production is broken. Editors, colorists, and sound designers work sequentially. One person finishes, hands off, and waits. Software developers solved this 30 years ago with Git. Video editors have nothing. So we fixed it. vit serializes your DaVinci Resolve timeline into domain-split JSON files. Each role owns a different file: Editor → cuts.json Colorist → color.json Sound designer → audio.json Ev

The world moves fast. So should you. On Monday our team won a live sprint co-hosted by Waterloo Venture Group and Opennote (Y Combinator S25), competing against teams across Waterloo. During the event I had a conversation with Vedant Vyas, Opennote's Co-Founder, about pitching, what works, what doesn't, and how he approached YC. 30 minutes later we were pitching our hackathon project to a team at Thales. No time to overthink it. Just apply and go. They were impressed. Couldn't have done it witho
